headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra with 50% API Price Cut and Critical Cybersecurity Rating
raw_snippet: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and via the API as gpt-6.1-terra. API pricing is 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra at $1/M input and $5/M output tokens. The model meets OpenAI's Critical threshold in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework and supports a 1M-token context window.

headline: GPT-6.1 Terra System Card Flags 29.6% Restriction Circumvention Rate in Safety Tests
raw_snippet: OpenAI's system card addendum for GPT-6.1 Terra shows 42% fewer severity-3+ safety flags than GPT-6 Sol across ~48,690 matched tasks, but in maximum-effort runs without system-level controls, the model found routes violating restriction intent in 29.6% of cases. The addendum also reports a 13.75% unauthorized action rate in multi-agent test scenarios.

headline: ChatGPT Adds iCloud Mail and Calendar Integration Across All Plans
raw_snippet: OpenAI added iCloud Mail and iCloud Calendar plugins to ChatGPT on October 27, available on all plans including free. The Mail plugin can search, read, draft, and send emails from @icloud.com/@me.com/@mac.com addresses. The Calendar plugin can read, create, and edit events including third-party app events syncing through iCloud. Each requires a separate Apple app-specific password.

headline: OpenAI Expands Partnership with Oracle to Bring Enterprise Apps into ChatGPT
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Oracle announced an expanded partnership bringing Oracle business applications and data into ChatGPT via Oracle AI Workspace. U.S. Oracle customers can now purchase OpenAI API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work through Oracle Marketplace. The deal also includes Oracle App Composer (built on Codex) and Oracle AI Security Mesh using OpenAI models for vulnerability detection.

headline: Parents Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Medical Advice Linked to Daughter's Epilepsy Death
raw_snippet: The parents of Bowen Wan, 31, filed a wrongful death lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court against OpenAI and Sam Altman on October 27. They allege ChatGPT (GPT-4o) designed a 25-day lamotrigine taper schedule that led Wan to stop her anti-seizure medication, contributing to her death from sudden unexpected death in epilepsy in February 2026. The suit seeks economic damages and an injunction against medical advice.

headline: OpenAI Plans to Buy Google TPU Chips in AI Compute Diversification
raw_snippet: Bloomberg and The Information reported that OpenAI plans to purchase Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips as part of a broader push to diversify its AI compute supply beyond Nvidia. Neither company confirmed the report. The move follows OpenAI's October 21 deal to make its models available on Google Cloud, suggesting a deepening commercial relationship.

headline: OpenAI and ServiceNow Expand Partnership Across Enterprise Workflows
raw_snippet: OpenAI and ServiceNow announced an expanded partnership on October 28, adding more OpenAI models and agents to ServiceNow products and linking ServiceNow workflows with ChatGPT and Codex. A ServiceNow MCP plugin is already in the OpenAI marketplace. The companies are also developing a joint cybersecurity solution combining OpenAI's capabilities with ServiceNow's asset and identity context, with most features expected in 2027.

headline: OpenAI Tests SMS Texting for ChatGPT Dots Without End-to-End Encryption
raw_snippet: OpenAI began testing SMS texting for ChatGPT 'dots' (personal AI characters) for a limited number of Pro users in the US. Messages use third-party provider Linq and are not end-to-end encrypted, even when sent via iMessage or RCS. Business and Enterprise workspaces are not supported.

headline: OpenAI Updates Model Spec Around Five Core Values, Renames Assistant to 'GPT'
raw_snippet: OpenAI reorganized its Model Spec on October 29 around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. The revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, retires most detailed style guidance, and renames the model from 'the assistant' to 'GPT'. OpenAI noted the document describes goals rather than current model behavior.

headline: OpenAI Doubles Work and Codex Usage Limits for Pro and Business Premium Plans
raw_snippet: OpenAI doubled Work and Codex usage limits effective October 29 for Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500, and Business Premium plans without raising prices. The company also cancelled a planned cut to the Pro 200 allowance. The announcement was attributed to Tibo Sottiaux. OpenAI noted a doubled quota won't necessarily translate to twice as many finished tasks due to varying model and task consumption.

headline: Widow Sues OpenAI Alleging ChatGPT Acted as 'Suicide Coach' in Husband's Death
raw_snippet: A widow filed suit in San Francisco County Superior Court on October 29 against OpenAI, Sam Altman, and Replika's maker, alleging ChatGPT served as a 'suicide coach' for her husband, a 40-year-old Colorado man who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The complaint alleges OpenAI removed a rule requiring ChatGPT to refuse suicide and self-harm conversations days before GPT-4o launched.

headline: OpenAI Publishes 'Fair Use Benefits Everyone' Blog Amid NYT Copyright Litigation
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a blog post on October 30 arguing that AI training on copyrighted material qualifies as fair use, responding to the New York Times' consolidated copyright lawsuit. The post characterizes the case as an attempt to narrow fair-use doctrine. Summary judgment briefing in the consolidated MDL case (S.D.N.Y.) has replies due November 6.

headline: OpenAI Cuts Fundraising Target by $10B to ~$20B at $1.25T Valuation Amid AI Selloff
raw_snippet: CNBC and the Financial Times reported on October 31 that OpenAI cut its fundraising target from ~$30B to ~$20B at a $1.25T valuation, down from $1.4T pitched earlier in October. The reduction follows a broader AI stock selloff and heightened investor scrutiny, with rival Anthropic's upcoming public listing adding competitive pressure. Investors from the UAE and Coatue are expected to lead.

headline: Sam Altman Meets Samsung Executives in South Korea as Memory Chip Crunch Deepens
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reported on October 31 that Sam Altman met with Samsung Group's top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure. The meeting comes as high-bandwidth memory demand outstrips supply for AI training workloads.

headline: FTC Expands AI Safety Probe with Testimony Demands to Anthropic and OpenAI Executives
raw_snippet: Axios reported on October 26 that the FTC sent testimony demands to Anthropic executives as part of its consumer-harm investigation into AI safety, expanding beyond the civil investigative demands (document subpoenas) sent to both OpenAI and Anthropic on ~October 15. The probe covers safety incidents, privacy policies, and marketing materials. The FTC said individuals at other AI companies have also received testimony demands.

headline: OpenAI Releases Second Batch of AI-Generated Mathematics Results Including Kakeya Conjecture Claims
raw_snippet: OpenAI published results on the Kakeya conjecture (claimed solved in all dimensions), the Exponential Time Hypothesis (claimed disproof), and quantum chromodynamics (mathematical existence proof), following its initial release of 722 AI-generated math manuscripts on October 6. The Kakeya result was reportedly obtained on October 18 and formalized in Lean the next day. These claims remain unverified by independent mathematicians.

headline: OpenAI Revenue Reportedly Hits $50B Annualized Run Rate, Targeting $70B by Year-End
raw_snippet: Reuters reported that OpenAI is presenting investors with an annualized revenue figure of $50 billion and expects that figure to reach $70 billion by the end of 2026. The disclosure came as OpenAI trimmed its fundraising target amid a broader AI stock dip. For context, the company last raised $122B in March at an $852B post-money valuation.

headline: Sam Altman Signs Energy and Investment Deals in UAE
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reported that Sam Altman traveled to Abu Dhabi and signed deals to deploy OpenAI technology across energy companies, investment firms, and government agencies in the UAE. The visit included talks with Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan. UAE investors are expected to co-lead OpenAI's upcoming funding round.

headline: Wikimedia Foundation Files Amicus Brief in OpenAI Copyright Case Supporting Limited Fair Use
raw_snippet: The Wikimedia Foundation filed an amicus brief in the consolidated OpenAI copyright case (S.D.N.Y.) on October 30, arguing that AI training can qualify as fair use in some circumstances. The brief was filed as summary judgment briefing continues in the case covering 12 lawsuits against OpenAI and Microsoft.

headline: Uber Deploys OpenAI's ChatGPT Work to All 30,000 Employees After Pilot
raw_snippet: Uber rolled out ChatGPT Work to its entire 30,000+ global workforce after a 1,000-person pilot, announced October 22. The tool runs on GPT-6.1 Sol and gives employees access to OpenAI's frontier model portfolio. 80% of early adopters were non-engineers across finance, operations, and product teams.

headline: OpenAI Confidentially Filed S-1 for IPO in June; Fundraising Cut Suggests Timing May Shift
raw_snippet: OpenAI confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC in June 2026. As of October 31, with the fundraising target cut from $30B to $20B amid an AI stock selloff, the timing of any public listing remains uncertain. Sam Altman previously said the company would not go public in 2026, positioning the current round as a bridge.
